messages:
maggie: heads-up: prototyping a 'predictive burn' chart for the console. shows projected token spend for next 7/30 days based on current model mix + a simple forecast if we switch X% traffic to a cheaper model. also overlays estimated cache savings. WIP PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/console/pull/789 Thoughts before I wire it to the backend?
evam: love this. can we surface margin per-model (e.g., $/k tokens) and the incremental delta when changing routing?
sachin: we need to be careful about sampling bias — dashboards use 1% trace sampling in prod; projection needs to inflate properly for sample rate. currently our naive approach multiplies by 100 which is noisy for tail models.
amanda: @sachin good call. maybe compute a model-pop-weighted scaling factor on a monthly cadence and use that to stabilize day-to-day projections. remembered we sketched a 'sample-aware extrapolation' metric last quarter.
evam: also UX note: customers want a 'what-if' slider for % traffic shift and see the line chart update in <200ms. can we precompute per-sku curves or cached delta buckets? incremental cache savings estimation could be approximated rather than exact.
maggie: backend plan: add a lightweight preview endpoint POST /v1/preview-burn that accepts {route, shift_percent, horizon_days, ramp:'instant'|'30d'} and returns per-day tokens + estimated cache_savings + p10/p90 bands. will rely on aggregation tables with a sample_scale factor. pseudo: ```POST /preview-burn {"route":"/v1/generate","shift":20} ```
sachin: watch out for granularity — our aggregation tables are (route, model_sku, hour). to estimate cache delta we need join to cached_prefix_hits and estimate unique-prefix overlap. that's the tricky part.
deploy-bot: deploy: analytics-api v2.13 merged to prod (hash abc123) — includes new preview endpoint schema.
amanda: :thumbsup: can we add a confidence band (p10/p90) to make it clear this is a projection? that helps sales/finance when planning budgets.
evam: agree. suggest bootstrap CI from last 30 days for bands; cheap and interpretable.
maggie: OK i'll add p10/p90 and a tooltip that explains sampling scaling, assumptions (no model behavior change), and cache-estimation caveats. tagging @analytics for a quick data review before prod.
sachin: one more: if sticky routing is enabled, the "what-if" should show both immediate reroute and a 30d gradual ramp option (sticky = percent of users stick to original path). modeling needs that dimension.
maggie: good call — will add a ramp toggle + note about sticky effects. thanks all, i'll open the UI + backend PR tomorrow and drop a short demo gif in #product.
